source_findings.finding: The Codex app is framed around supervising multiple agents, long-running work, app/CLI continuity, skills, and automations.
source_findings.application: Use watcher/notifier supervision to let sibling lanes run while Aletheon prepares source, eureka, and x2 build work.

source_findings.finding: Release movement means CLI/App helper assumptions should be captured as receipts rather than hidden in ad hoc state.
source_findings.application: Keep launch, completion, quality, redaction, exposure, and dashboard receipts modular and phase-scoped.

source_findings.finding: Layered controls, review boundaries, and cautious tool operation are core to safe agentic work.
source_findings.application: Continue exact staging, drift checks, status-only publication, and open empirical gates.

source_findings.finding: Least authority and confused-deputy avoidance matter when multiple tools or connectors interact.
source_findings.application: Keep app, CLI, connector, and repository surfaces separated by explicit receipts and mutation boundaries.

source_findings.finding: Logs and diagnostics can expose sensitive data when raw material is retained or published.
source_findings.application: Keep raw sibling output temp-only and publish only hashes, counts, pass/fail statuses, and sanitized summaries.

x2_build_implications: Use the v3 x1 launch receipts to prove watcher-trust cadence without polling before the gate.
Use official Codex app guidance to justify dashboarded multi-agent status surfaces.
Keep CLI long-form quality gates separate from raw output publication.
Treat app completion redaction as a serial precondition before app gate publication.
Keep all GMUT, canon, consciousness, and final-physics gates open unless exact closure artifacts exist.
